mainTopic: גזל הגר: who receives the payment, including a female convert and a כהן who is himself the robber
overview: The גמרא first challenges רבא's explanation, which seemed to let a robber forgive a debt to himself. If that were so, the Torah's law of giving גזל הגר to the כהנים could never happen. רבא answers that the law applies when the robber admits only after the convert has died, because then ה׳ acquires the debt and gives it to the כהנים. רבינא asks whether robbing a female convert is included. A ברייתא shows that she is, and that the word "איש" teaches that only an adult convert must be checked for heirs. Another ברייתא teaches that the payment goes to the כהנים of the משמר on duty. If the robber is himself a כהן, he cannot keep the payment; it is shared among all the כהנים. The גמרא tries to explain this as a case of a כהן טמא, rejects that answer, and instead learns it through a גזירה שוה from a redeemed שדה אחוזה. Finally, a ברייתא teaches that a כהן may offer his own קרבנות any time, and he keeps their service rights and hide even if he is a בעל מום.

steps.title: If the robber can forgive himself, when does the payment ever reach the כהנים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws an inference from רבא's explanation: according to רבי יוסי הגלילי, someone can forgive a debt even to himself. It then asks how the Torah's case of גזל הגר paid to the כהנים could ever happen.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it follows that רבי יוסי הגלילי holds a person can forgive the debt even to himself? But then the robbery of a convert, which the Torah says must be given to the כהנים, how could that case ever happen?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is attacking רבא's earlier explanation. It shows that this explanation leads to a problem with an explicit law in the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture a robber who stole from a convert, and the convert dies with no heirs. If the robber could simply forgive the debt to himself, he would never have to pay anyone. That would make the Torah's command to give the payment to the כהנים almost impossible to fulfill.

keyTerms.meaning: by inference; it follows from this that
to himself
he is able to forgive (a debt)
robbery of a convert who died without heirs, which is paid to the כהנים
how can you find such a case?

phrases.english: By inference, does it follow that Rabbi Yosei HaGelili holds:
that he can forgive it even to himself?!
But the robbery of a convert,
about which the Merciful One says it must be given to the priests,
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:8

phrases.english: how can you find such a case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's explanation from the previous section of the daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading of רבי יוסי הגלילי, which implies a person can forgive a debt to himself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If self-forgiveness works, a robber of a convert who dies could always cancel his own debt. The Torah's law of paying the כהנים would then never apply.

steps.title: The case where the robber admits only after the convert dies
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the Torah's case is when the robber swore falsely and admitted only after the convert died. At that moment ה׳ acquires the debt and gives it to the כהנים, so the robber can no longer forgive it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Here we are dealing with someone who robbed a convert and swore falsely to him. Then the convert died, and the robber admitted after the death. At the moment he admitted, ה׳ acquired the debt and gave it to the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his explanation. He narrows the Torah's law to one specific case where self-forgiveness does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key point is when the robber admits. If he admits after the convert is already dead, the right to the payment goes directly to ה׳, who passes it to the כהנים. The robber never holds that right, so he has nothing to forgive.

keyTerms.meaning: what case are we dealing with here?
and he swore (falsely) to him
and he admitted
ה׳ acquired it

steps.whatToRemember: גזל הגר goes to the כהנים when the robber admits after the convert's death. At that moment ה׳ acquires the debt and gives it to the כהנים.

phrases.english: Rava said: With what are we dealing here?
Where he robbed the convert and swore to him,
phrases.notes: He swore falsely that he never robbed him.

phrases.english: and the convert died, and he admitted after the death;
so that at the time he admitted,
the Name acquired it and gave it to the priests.
phrases.notes: "The Name" means ה׳.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any robbery of a convert who dies could be forgiven by the robber, so the כהנים would never receive anything.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the robber admits after the death, the debt goes straight to ה׳ and the כהנים, so he cannot forgive it.

steps.title: Does the law also apply to robbing a female convert?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks about robbing a female convert who dies without heirs. Does the payment also go to the כהנים, or does the word "איש" in the פסוק limit the law to a man?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא asked: What is the law about robbing a female convert? The Torah says "איש," a man, so maybe a woman is not included. Or perhaps the פסוק simply speaks in its usual male wording?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a question. It asks whether the law of גזל הגר also covers a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to read "איש." It could be a real limit, meaning only a man. Or it could just be the Torah's normal way of speaking, which uses male language even when women are included too.

keyTerms.meaning: he asked (raised a question)
a female convert
or perhaps
the usual way the פסוק speaks

steps.confusionAlert: רבינא is not saying women are excluded. He is asking whether "איש" is a real limit or just ordinary Torah wording.

phrases.english: Ravina asked: Robbery of a female convert, what is the law?
The Merciful One said "man," and not a woman,
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:8

phrases.english: or perhaps it is just the way the verse speaks?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question after the previous discussion ends.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the payment for robbing a female convert who dies without heirs also goes to the כהנים.

steps.title: רב אהרן brings a ברייתא that includes a woman
steps.stepSummary: רב אהרן answers רבינא by quoting a ברייתא. It asks where we learn that a woman is included, and it begins answering from the word "המושב."
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אהרן said to רבינא: Come and hear, as a ברייתא teaches: "איש" alone would only teach about a man. Where do we learn about a woman? When the פסוק says "המושב," there are two here...
steps.whatsHappening: רב אהרן is bringing a source to settle רבינא's question. The ברייתא goes on in steps 5–6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא agrees that "איש" alone would only teach about a man. It then finds an extra mention of "המושב" in the פסוק and uses it to include a woman. This answers רבינא: a female convert is included.

keyTerms.meaning: I would only know
from where do we learn?
that is returned (the payment that is given back)

phrases.english: Rav Aharon said to Ravina:
Come and hear, as it is taught in a baraita:
"Man": I would only know about a man;
from where do we learn about a woman?
When it says "that is returned,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:8

phrases.english: there are two here,
phrases.notes: The פסוק mentions returning the payment twice. The extra mention is what brings in a woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַהֲרֹן לְרָבִינָא: תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבינא's question in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That robbing a female convert who dies without heirs is also paid to the כהנים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that uses the extra mention of "המושב" in במדבר 5:8 to include a woman.

steps.title: If a woman is included, why does the verse say "man"?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא challenges itself: if the word המושב already includes a woman, what is the word "איש" coming to teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the Torah teaching us by saying "man"?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא has just shown that a woman is included, so now it asks why the פסוק uses the word "איש" at all. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once המושב includes a woman, "איש" can no longer be read as limiting the law to men. The ברייתא assumes no word in the Torah is extra, so "איש" must teach something else.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if what we just said is true
What does the verse come to teach? (said when a word looks extra)
Man; the word in the פסוק being explained

phrases.english: If so, what does the verse teach by saying "man"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the derivation from המושב by asking what the word "איש" then teaches.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a woman is included, the word "איש" seems to have nothing left to teach.

steps.title: "Man" teaches when you must check for relatives
steps.stepSummary: "איש" teaches that for a grown convert you must check whether he has relatives. For a child convert there is no need to check, since he certainly has none.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a man, you have to look into whether he has relatives or not. With a child, you don't have to look into it. It is known that he has no relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that "איש" is not about men versus women. It teaches about checking whether the convert left any relatives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An adult convert may have had children after converting, so the robber must find out whether there is an heir before paying the כהנים. A child convert cannot have children, so it is already clear that the payment goes to the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: To look into him; to investigate
Relatives who would inherit (the פסוק's word for heirs)
A minor; a child
It is known; it is certain

steps.whatToRemember: A woman convert is included in גזל הגר. The word "איש" teaches only that an adult convert must be checked for heirs, while a child convert obviously has none.

phrases.english: For a man, you need to look into him

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ לוֹ גּוֹאֲלִים אִם לָאו,
phrases.english: whether he has relatives or not,

phrases.aramaic: קָטָן אִי אַתָּה צָרִיךְ לַחֲזוֹר אַחֲרָיו;
phrases.english: for a minor, you do not need to look into him;
it is known that he has no relatives.
phrases.notes: A convert has no family from before he converted, and a child is too young to have children of his own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by giving "איש" a new meaning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the word a different purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "איש" would seem to leave out a woman, or to be an extra word.
steps.terutzMaskana: "איש" teaches that an adult must be checked for heirs and a child need not be.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The answer to רבינא's question is that a woman convert's case also goes to the כהנים.

steps.title: ה׳ acquires the payment and gives it to the כהן on duty
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches from "לה' לכהן" that ה׳ acquires the payment and gives it to the כהן of the משמר serving at that time.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: "To ה׳, to the כהן" means that ה׳ acquired it and gave it to the כהן of that משמר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא opens a new topic: which כהנים get the payment for גזל הגר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "לה'" teach that ה׳ first takes ownership, which matches what רבא said earlier. The words "לכהן" teach that ה׳ passes it to the כהנים of the משמר on duty, not to just any כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: ה׳ acquired it
A group of כהנים who served in the מקדש during a set week

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"To Hashem, to the כהן" —
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:8

phrases.english: ה׳ acquired it,
and gave it to the כהן of that watch.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא about who receives the payment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The payment goes to the כהן of the משמר on duty.

steps.title: Maybe any כהן he wants may receive it?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the payment really must go to the משמר on duty, or whether the robber may give it to any כהן he chooses.
steps.simpleTranslation: You say it goes to the כהן of that watch. Or maybe it can go to any כהן he wants?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא questions its own rule and asks for proof. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "לכהן" alone could mean any כהן at all. So the ברייתא needs a source that limits it to the משמר on duty.

keyTerms.meaning: You say (opens a question about a derived rule)
Or perhaps it is only
That he wants; of his choosing

phrases.english: You say to the כהן of that watch;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְכׇל כֹּהֵן שֶׁיִּרְצֶה?
phrases.english: or perhaps it is to any כהן he wants?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how we know the rule just stated.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the payment is limited to the משמר on duty.

steps.title: Proof from the ram of atonement
steps.stepSummary: The same פסוק mentions the איל הכפורים, which the כהן on duty offers. This shows that the money also goes to the כהן of that משמר.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the verse says "besides the ram of atonement, with which he will atone for him," it shows that the verse is talking about the כהן of that watch.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers by pointing to the end of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ram can only be brought by the כהן serving in the מקדש at that time. Since the money is mentioned together with the ram, it goes to the same כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: When it says (introduces a proof from a פסוק)
The ram of atonement brought by the robber
The verse is speaking about

phrases.english: When it says

phrases.aramaic: ״מִלְּבַד אֵיל הַכִּפֻּרִים אֲשֶׁר יְכַפֶּר בּוֹ עָלָיו״ –
phrases.english: "Besides the ram of atonement, with which he will atone for him" —
phrases.notes: This is the end of the same פסוק, במדבר 5:8. The ram is offered by the כהן who is on duty.

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי לַכֹּהֵן שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ מִשְׁמָר הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר.
phrases.english: so the verse is speaking of the כהן of that watch.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר ״מִלְּבַד אֵיל הַכִּפֻּרִים אֲשֶׁר יְכַפֶּר בּוֹ עָלָיו״

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The money goes with the ram to the כהן on duty.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Payment for גזל הגר goes to the כהנים of the משמר serving at that time.

steps.title: A כהן who robbed a convert: can he say "it's mine"?
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא discusses a robber who is himself a כהן. Since the payment goes to כהנים and it is already in his hands, may he claim it for himself?
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If the robber was a כהן, from where do we know that he should not say, "Since it goes to the כהנים and it is in my hands, let it be mine"?
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא opens a new case: what happens when the robber is a כהן. It sets up the argument that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the robber hands the payment over to the כהנים. Here the robber is a כהן himself, so the question is whether the money can simply stay with him.

keyTerms.meaning: Robber; one who robs
From where do we know?
Since; because
In my hands; in my possession

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If the robber was a כהן,
from where do we know that he should not say:
"Since it goes out to the כהנים,

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲרֵי הוּא תַּחַת יָדִי – יְהֵא שֶׁלִּי?
phrases.english: and it is in my hands — let it be mine"?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיָה גּוֹזֵל כֹּהֵן, מִנַּיִן שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the rule that the payment goes to the כהנים to raise a new case: the robber is a כהן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a כהן robber may keep the payment for himself.

steps.title: Logic says he should keep it: a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives a קל וחומר: if a כהן can acquire payments owed by other robbers, he should all the more acquire the one he himself owes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is logical: if he acquires what belongs to others, then what is his own, all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא lays out a logical argument that the כהן should be able to keep the money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As a כהן he can receive payments for גזל הגר from other robbers. A payment that is already in his own hands should be even easier for him to keep.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is logical (introduces a reasoned argument)
Acquires; has a right to
All the more so (a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: And it is logical:
if he acquires what belongs to others,
what is his own — not all the more so?
phrases.notes: "Others" means payments from other robbers that he gets as a כהן. "His own" is the payment he himself owes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a logical argument about the claim raised in the question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a כהן robber must hand over the payment
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from other robbers' payments to his own payment suggests he keeps it.

steps.title: רבי נתן's version of the same argument
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן puts the logic differently. If no one can take away something a כהן had no share in until he received it, then surely no one can take away something he already had a share in.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן says it in different words: Take something in which he has no share until it comes into his possession. Once it comes into his possession, no one can take it out of his hand. So with something in which he has a share even before it comes into his possession, once it has come in, isn't it logical that no one else can take it from his hand?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן gives a second way of stating the same argument that the כהן keeps the money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison is to a gift any כהן may receive, which belongs to no one until it is given. A כהן of the משמר already has a share in the גזל הגר payment, so once it is in his hands, his claim is even stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: In different words
A share; a portion
His possession; his domain
To take it out of his hand

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says it in different words:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק בּוֹ
phrases.english: Now, if something in which he has no share
until it comes into his possession —
once it comes into his possession,
[another] cannot take it out of his hand;
phrases.notes: The ברייתא doesn't name an example. He means something any כהן could be given, like תרומה.

phrases.english: then something in which he has a share
even before it comes into his possession —
once it has come into his possession,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין דְּאֵין אַחֵר יָכוֹל לְהוֹצִיאוֹ מִיָּדוֹ?
phrases.english: isn't it logical that no one else can take it out of his hand?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates the קל וחומר of the previous step in different words.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a כהן robber must hand over the payment
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If no one can take away a gift that was not his until received, then surely no one can take away something he already had a share in.

steps.title: The comparison fails: everyone shares in stolen property
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the קל וחומר. Something like תרומה belongs to no כהן until one receives it, so no one else has a claim on it. But every כהן of the משמר already has a share in the robbery payment, so the robber must give it up to be shared.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. You can say that about something he had no share in, because just as he had no share, no one else did either. But would you say that about stolen property? Just as he has a share in it, others also have a share in it. Rather, the stolen item is taken from him and divided among all his fellow כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא knocks down the קל וחומר from steps 11–12. It concludes that the robber-כהן must hand over what he stole so all the כהנים can share it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר assumed that already having a share makes his claim stronger. The ברייתא turns this around. When no one had a share, whoever grabs it first keeps it. But here every כהן in the משמר already has a share, so the robber's share does not push out theirs.

keyTerms.meaning: A share or portion
Stolen property
Others (the other כהנים)
Is divided up

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן who robbed a גר does not keep the payment himself. It is divided among all the כהנים.
steps.confusionAlert: Having a share does not mean owning the whole thing. Because the others also have a share, he cannot claim it all.

phrases.english: No; if you said this

steps.title: A challenge from 'his holy things shall be his'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ruling. The פסוק says a man's holy things belong to him, so the robber-כהן should keep the payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'And every man's holy things shall be his'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ruling of step 13 with a פסוק. The פסוק seems to say that a כהן keeps his own holy things for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק suggests that a כהן who brings his own offering keeps its portions. If so, the robber-כהן should also keep the payment for his own robbery. This clashes with the ruling that it must be shared.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written
Holy things (offerings and gifts)

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
'And every man's holy things shall be his'!
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:10

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the robber-כהן must share the payment
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says a man's holy things are his own, so he should keep it

steps.title: Answer: the case is a כהן טמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a כהן טמא. He cannot serve, so he gets no share.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we dealing with here? With a כהן טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by limiting the ברייתא to a כהן who is טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'his holy things shall be his' applies to a כהן who can serve. A כהן טמא cannot bring the offering. So the פסוק does not help him, and the payment goes to the other כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?
A ritually impure כהן

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
With a כהן who is טמא
phrases.notes: A טמא כהן can't do the עבודה, so he doesn't get a share of the offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about any כהן, which clashes with the פסוק
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is only about a כהן טמא, who has no share

steps.title: A כהן טמא has no share at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer. The ברייתא said the robber has a share in it, but a כהן טמא has no share.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is a כהן טמא, does he have 'a thing in which he has a share'?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer of step 15, using the ברייתא's own words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא described the payment as 'a thing in which he has a share' (step 12, echoed in step 13). A כהן טמא has no share, so the ברייתא cannot be talking about him. The answer of step 15 does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Does he have it?

phrases.english: If it is about a כהן טמא,
'a thing in which he has a share'
does he have that?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the case is a כהן טמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the robber has a share, but a כהן טמא has none

steps.title: New answer: a גזירה שוה from שדה אחוזה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new source. The word 'לכהן' appears both here and by שדה אחוזה. So the law of the field teaches the law of the robbery.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is learned from 'לכהן'–'לכהן' from שדה אחוזה.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the כהן טמא answer, the גמרא gives a different reason why the robber-כהן must share. It uses a גזירה שוה with שדה אחוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the ברייתא can be about any כהן, even a טהור one. The rule does not come from his being unable to serve. It comes from a word match with the field law, which the גמרא will explain next.

keyTerms.meaning: It is learned (by comparison)
Learning one law from another through a shared word
A field inherited from one's ancestors

phrases.english: Rather, it is learned from 'to the כהן'–'to the כהן'
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:8 and ויקרא 27:21; the same word appears in both places.

phrases.english: from an inherited field

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 15 with a new source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא must be about a כהן טמא
steps.terutzMaskana: Any כהן must share, learned from שדה אחוזה

steps.title: The ברייתא about a כהן who redeemed the field
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא about a field that goes to the כהנים at יובל. One כהן redeemed it before then. Can he say it is his because it is already in his hands?
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'His possession' — why does the פסוק say this? Take a field that goes to the כהנים at יובל, and one of the כהנים redeemed it. How do we know he may not say: since it goes to the כהנים at יובל, and it is already in my hands, it should be mine?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins quoting the source for the גזירה שוה. It sets up the field case, which matches our robbery case. The answer comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The field case is just like the robber-כהן. A כהן holds something that belongs to all the כהנים and wants to keep it because it is already in his hands. The ברייתא asks how we know he cannot do that, and the word 'אחזתו' will give the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the פסוק need to say this?
The fiftieth year, when fields go back
He redeemed it
Since

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the source for the robbery case. Whatever it rules about the כהן who holds the field will apply to the כהן who robbed the גר.

phrases.english: As it was taught: 'His possession'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:21

phrases.english: why does the פסוק say this?
How do we know, about a field that goes out
to the כהנים at יובל
and one of the כהנים redeemed it
how do we know he may not say:
Since it goes out to the כהנים at יובל,
and here it is in my hands,
it should be mine?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind the גזירה שוה of step 17
steps.raayaObject: That a כהן holding something owed to all the כהנים cannot keep it for himself
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on 'אחזתו' about a שדה אחוזה redeemed by a כהן

steps.title: A logical argument that the כהן should keep the field
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא offers a קל וחומר: if a כהן gets fields that belonged to others, surely he keeps a field that is his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it makes sense: if I acquire a field that belonged to other people, then a field that is mine, is it not all the more so?!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues from step 18. It gives a logical reason (a קל וחומר) why the כהן who redeemed the field should keep it. This sets up the next step, where the פסוק will reject the idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At יובל, כהנים receive fields that once belonged to other people. This כהן redeemed the field himself, so it is already 'his own.' The logic says that if he gets what is not his, he should surely keep what is his.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument (here, a reasoning from logic rather than a פסוק)
All the more so: the conclusion of a קל וחומר
I acquire, I gain ownership

phrases.english: And it is logical:
if I acquire with regard to a field belonging to others,
with regard to my own, is it not all the more so?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the logical basis for the claim raised in step 18, that the redeeming כהן keeps the field.
steps.raayaObject: That the כהן who redeemed the field keeps it at יובל
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from fields of others that כהנים acquire

steps.title: The פסוק shows the field is split among all the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'אחזתו' teaches that only an inherited field is his. A redeemed field leaves his hands and is divided among all the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק teaches: 'As a field dedicated, his possession shall be to the כהן.' An inherited possession is his, but this field is not his. How so? It leaves his hands and is divided among all his brother כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the קל וחומר using a פסוק. The redeemed field does not stay with the כהן; all the כהנים share it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אחזתו' (his possession) limits ownership to a field the כהן inherited. A field he redeemed does not count as 'his possession', so the logic fails. Through the גזירה שוה of 'לכהן' from step 17, a robbery payment the robber-כהן owes also leaves his hands and goes to all the כהנים of that משמר.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches: introduces a verse that settles the question
A dedicated field that goes to the כהנים at יובל
An ancestral possession (inherited land)

steps.whatToRemember: Even when the property is already in the כהן's hands, he does not keep it. It is shared by all the כהנים, and the גזירה שוה applies the same rule to the robbery payment.
steps.whyThisMatters: This completes the source from step 17. It explains why the robber-כהן cannot keep the payment for himself.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"As a field dedicated, the possession thereof shall be to the כהן"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:21

phrases.english: a possession is his,
phrases.notes: He means a field the כהן inherited from his family.

phrases.english: but this one is not his.
How so?
It leaves his possession,
and is divided among all his brothers, the כהנים.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: כִּשְׂדֵה הַחֵרֶם לַכֹּהֵן תִּהְיֶה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of step 19 using a פסוק.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The logical argument that the redeeming כהן keeps the field
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק limits 'his possession' to an inherited field. A redeemed field is not included.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The field is divided among all the כהנים, and by the גזירה שוה so is the robbery payment.

steps.title: A כהן may bring his own קרבנות any time
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא teaches from a פסוק that a כהן may come and offer his own קרבנות whenever he wishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: From where do we know that a כהן may come and offer his קרבנות at any time and any hour he wants? The פסוק says: 'And he comes with all the desire of his soul… and he shall serve.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new ברייתא about a כהן's rights to his own קרבנות. It first teaches that he does not have to wait for his משמר's week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally each משמר of כהנים serves only in its own week. This ברייתא learns from 'בכל אות נפשו' that a כהן offering his own קרבן may serve whenever he wants. This sets the stage for the next part, which deals with the meat and hide.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
The desire of his soul: whenever he wants
And he shall serve (do the עבודה)

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
From where is it derived for a כהן
that he may come and offer his own offerings
at any time and at any hour that he wishes?
The verse states:
"And he comes with all the desire of his soul," "then he shall serve."
phrases.notes: דברים 18:6–7

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִנַּיִן לְכֹהֵן שֶׁבָּא וּמַקְרִיב קׇרְבְּנוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא about a כהן's rights to his own קרבנות, connected to the earlier discussion of 'ואיש את קדשיו לו יהיו'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן may offer his own קרבנות at any time, even outside his משמר.

steps.title: The service and hide of his קרבן belong to him
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from 'ואיש את קדשיו לו יהיו' that the service and the hide of a כהן's own קרבן are his.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that its service and its hide are his? The פסוק says: 'And every man's holy things shall be his.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues. It teaches that when a כהן brings his own קרבן, the service and the hide stay with him and do not go to the משמר on duty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same פסוק the גמרא quoted in step 14. Here it is used to show that a כהן keeps the service rights of his own קרבן and its hide.

keyTerms.meaning: The service of the קרבן, with the rights that come with it
The hide (skin) of the animal
His holy things (his קרבנות)

phrases.english: And from where is it derived that its service and its hide are his?
phrases.notes: "Its service" means the rights that come with doing the service, like eating the meat.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"And every man's holy things shall be his."
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:10, the same פסוק from step 14.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second rule to the ברייתא of step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The service and hide of a כהן's own קרבן belong to him.

steps.title: Even a כהן with a מום keeps the service and hide
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains the case: a כהן with a מום gives his קרבן to a כהן of the משמר on duty, yet the service and hide still belong to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If he was a בעל מום, he gives it to a כהן of that משמר, and its service and its hide are his.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains when this rule matters. It is the case of a כהן with a מום, who cannot do the service himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think a כהן who cannot serve loses his rights to the קרבן. The ברייתא says no: another כהן does the offering, but the owner-כהן still keeps the service rights and the hide.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? Introduces an explanation of the case
A כהן with a physical blemish, who may not serve
A priestly watch: the group of כהנים serving that week

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן's own קרבן belongs to him. Even a בעל מום who cannot offer it keeps the service rights and the hide.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the כהן טמא from step 15–16. A טמא has no share at all, but a בעל מום does keep the service rights and hide of his own קרבן.

phrases.english: How so?
If he was blemished,
he gives it to a כהן of that watch,
phrases.notes: He means the משמר on duty at that time, which offers the קרבן for him.

phrases.english: and its service and its hide are his.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא כֵּיצַד? אִם הָיָה בַּעַל מוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the case in which the rule of step 22 applies.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what case is it needed to say the service and hide belong to him?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When he is a בעל מום and another כהן offers his קרבן for him.
